prompt:
The inventory app in src/ has no notion of currency. Add a `currency` field to items and carry it through every layer: model.mjs, parser.mjs, validator.mjs, serializer.mjs, report.mjs and cli.mjs. Keep the existing file names and exports; src/index.mjs must also export `SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES`, `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`, `RATES_TO_USD`, `convert` and `renderSummary` (rules 8 to 11). New files are allowed.

Rules:

1. Supported currencies are USD, EUR, GBP, JPY and CAD. `SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES` is the array ["USD", "EUR", "GBP", "JPY", "CAD"] in that order and `DEFAULT_CURRENCY` is "USD".
2. Model: `createItem(raw, defaultCurrency = DEFAULT_CURRENCY)` returns an item that also has `currency`. The value is trimmed and uppercased. If `raw.currency` is missing, null or blank, the item gets `defaultCurrency` (uppercased).
3. Parser: the CSV may have an optional `currency` column in any position (header names stay case insensitive). `parseInventory(text, { defaultCurrency })` takes an optional second argument; blank cells and files without the column get that default, otherwise USD. Currency codes are uppercased by the parser, and an unknown code is kept and not rejected there.
4. Validator: an item without a currency (undefined) counts as USD. Any other currency must be exactly one of the supported codes (no normalizing, so "eur" or "" is invalid) or the error `currency must be one of USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD` is added. JPY has no decimals: for a JPY item whose price is otherwise a valid number but not an integer, add `price must be a whole number for JPY`. New errors go after the existing ones, the JPY price error before the currency error.
5. Serializer: `toCsv` writes the header `sku,name,qty,price,currency` (currency is always the last column) and formats each price with 2 decimals, or 0 decimals for JPY. `toJson` writes the keys in the order sku, name, qty, price, currency, with the price still a number. In both, an item that has no currency is written as USD.
6. Report: each item line becomes `SKU | Name | 3 x 19.99 USD = 59.97 USD` (amounts use the same decimals rule, then a space and the code). The single `Total:` line is replaced by one line per currency, `Total (EUR): 10.00`, in alphabetical order of the code and with the amount formatted for that currency, still followed by `Items: N`. An item without a currency is reported as USD, and a report with no items has no total lines.
7. CLI: add `--currency CODE` (also `--currency=CODE`). It sets the default currency for rows whose currency is blank or missing; rows that name a currency keep it. The code is uppercased first. An unsupported code makes `run` return exit code 2 with stderr `unsupported currency: <CODE>` (uppercased), and `--currency` with no value gives exit code 2 and `missing value for --currency`. The usage text becomes exactly `usage: inventory <file> [--format csv|json|report|summary] [--currency CODE] [--total-in CODE]`. Validation errors keep the format `line N: message` with N the line number in the file, so a blank currency cell under `--currency JPY` with a price of 2.5 reports `price must be a whole number for JPY`.

8. Conversion: `RATES_TO_USD` is the object { USD: 1, EUR: 1.08, GBP: 1.27, JPY: 0.0067, CAD: 0.74 }, what one unit of each currency is worth in USD. `convert(amount, from, to)` returns the amount in the currency `to`, worked out as amount * RATES_TO_USD[from] / RATES_TO_USD[to] and rounded to the nearest unit of the decimals of `to` (cents, or whole yen for JPY), as a number. Both codes are trimmed and uppercased first. If a code is not supported, `convert` throws an Error whose message is `unsupported currency: <CODE>` (uppercased); `from` is checked before `to`.

9. Report totals in one currency: `renderReport(items, options = {})` takes an optional `options.totalIn` currency code. When it is given and there is at least one item, one more line `Total in <CODE>: <amount>` goes after the per currency total lines and before `Items: N`. The amount is the sum, over the per currency totals in alphabetical order of the code, of `convert(total, code, CODE)`, where each total is the unrounded sum of quantity times price for that currency, formatted with the decimals of CODE. The code is trimmed and uppercased, and an unsupported code throws the error from rule 8. With no items there is no such line.

10. Summary format: a new function `renderSummary(items, options = {})` returns JSON text (2 space indent, one newline at the end) for an object with the key `totals` first, an object that maps each currency code in alphabetical order to its total as a number rounded to the decimals of that currency, then the key `items` with the number of items, and then, only when `options.totalIn` is given and there is at least one item, the key `totalIn`, an object `{ "currency": CODE, "amount": N }` where N is the grand total from rule 9 as a number. An item without a currency counts as USD, and an unsupported totalIn throws the error from rule 8.

11. CLI: `--format summary` is a fourth format that prints `renderSummary(items, { totalIn })`. `--total-in CODE` (also `--total-in=CODE`) sets `totalIn` for the report and summary formats and has no effect on csv and json. The code is uppercased first. An unsupported code gives exit code 2 with stderr `unsupported currency: <CODE>`, checked after the `--currency` check, and `--total-in` with no value gives exit code 2 and `missing value for --total-in`. Validation errors are still reported with exit code 1 before any output is written.

The tests in test/ describe the old formats. Update them to the new behavior and add tests for the currency, conversion, summary and option rules. When you are done `npm test` must pass and test/ must hold at least 14 tests.
